messages:
oliver (support): Heads-up - customer reported function calls returning content from a different tool after last night's registry prune. attaching minimal repro and request ids.

oliver (support): example request id: req_20250328_9987, tool handle used: \`summarize_v2\`. response body contains output clearly from \`audio_transcribe_v1\`.

oliver (support): logs snippet:```
2025-03-28T04:12:03Z req=req_20250328_9987 selected_tool=uuid:7f3a2b handler=summarize_v2 resolved_alias=summarize_v2
2025-03-28T04:12:04Z req=req_20250328_9987 invoke_start uuid=3e9c1a handler=audio_transcribe_v1
```

oliver (support): customer page shows they called the alias, but runtime mapped to a different uuid. they said this started right after we pruned old aliases yesterday.

ops-bot: :rotating_light: registry-prune completed by deploy-bot at 2025-03-28T03:45:00Z. removed 242 stale aliases.

maria (eng-runtime): Thanks for the verbatim logs, Oliver. @sam can you take a look at the selection->invoke mapping? looks like alias resolution returned one uuid but the invocation table used a different row.

sam (eng-ml): Pulling logs. Two quick thoughts: 1) alias backfill process writes a temporary mapping set then prunes old rows; if rows were compacted by timestamp race we could pick the wrong uuid for similarly-named handles. 2) possible casefolding/unicode normalization collision if one handle had a soft-rename.

sam (eng-ml): Repro steps I'm trying:```
# reproduce locally
curl -X POST https://api.redwood/test-call -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"tool":"summarize_v2","input":"..."}'
# watch router logs for select -> invoke mapping
```

maria (eng-runtime): I checked DB history: alias `summarize_v2` was previously attached to uuid 3e9c1a (audio_transcribe_v1) in 2024-11, then reassigned to 7f3a2b in 2025-01. prune removed older tombstones at 03:45 which removed a last-write marker. That could allow a concurrent reader to see the older assignment if they hit a stale cache shard.

oliver (support): Customer-facing mitigation requested: can we advise them to call the tool via explicit uuid or temporary fallback to older version? they're on production and need immediate fix.

devex_jane (devex): quick mitigation: add the header `X-Tool-UUID: 7f3a2b` in calls to force the selection; also we can push a config to pin alias resolution TTL to 10m for that tenant.

sam (eng-ml): short-term I can add a router guard so that if select_uuid != invoke_uuid we abort and return 409 with diagnostic. That will fail fast instead of returning the wrong tool. deploy in 30m?

maria (eng-runtime): Yes please. Also we should roll back the prune tombstone removal to restore the last-write markers while we investigate. Ops - can we revert the prune?

ops-bot: revert-request submitted: revert-registry-prune/1748501234. ETA ~18 minutes.

oliver (support): I'll tell the customer to use `X-Tool-UUID` header and expect the router guard change. thanks team. :pray:

maria (eng-runtime): Follow-ups: 1) add a test for alias resolution race (concurrent reassignment + prune) 2) add stronger index on alias history to avoid tombstone loss on compaction 3) audit past prunes for similar patterns.

sam (eng-ml): logging action item: log both selected_alias_row_id and invoked_uuid in one correlated event so support can debug without tracing traces.

oliver (support): noted. closing loop with customer once revert and router-guard are live.
